extraction.name: C-EVAL: A Multi-Level Multi-Discipline Chinese Evaluation Suite for Foundation Models
extraction.description: C-EVAL is the first comprehensive Chinese evaluation suite designed to assess advanced knowledge and reasoning abilities of foundation models in a Chinese context. It comprises 13,948 multiple-choice questions across 52 diverse disciplines and four difficulty levels: middle school, high school, college, and professional. It also includes C-EVAL HARD, a subset of challenging subjects requiring advanced reasoning.
extraction.creator: Yuzhen Huang, Yuzhuo Bai, Zhihao Zhu, Junlei Zhang, Jinghan Zhang, Tangjun Su, Junteng Liu, Chuancheng Lv, Yikai Zhang, Jiayi Lei, Yao Fu, Maosong Sun, Junxian He
extraction.publisher: Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Tsinghua University, University of Edinburgh, The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology
extraction.citeAs: Huang, Y., Bai, Y., Zhu, Z., Zhang, J., Zhang, J., Su, T., Liu, J., Lv, C., Zhang, Y., Lei, J., Fu, Y., Sun, M., & He, J. (2023). C-EVAL: A Multi-Level Multi-Discipline Chinese Evaluation Suite for Foundation Models. arXiv preprint arXiv:2305.08322.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The data was collected from mock exams and small-scale local exams available online, as well as past exam questions from top universities in China and authorized questions from the Weipu website. The primary sources were PDF or Microsoft Word documents.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: PDF or Microsoft Word documents containing mock exams, local exam questions, and university past exam questions.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Questions were parsed into a structured format. Complex mathematical notations were manually converted to LaTeX. Questions with fewer than four options were eliminated, and questions with more than four options had incorrect choices randomly dropped to ensure exactly four choices. Deduplication and cleaning were performed.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Data was parsed from PDF/Word documents. LaTeX conversion was performed for STEM subjects. Questions were standardized to four choices. Deduplication and cleaning were applied. Human validation was conducted to ensure syntax correctness of LaTeX notations. Data was split into development, validation, and test sets.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The correct answers were provided in the source exam documents. For the development split, chain-of-thought explanations were generated by prompting GPT-4 and then manually revised by the authors.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: The authors of the paper performed manual annotation and validation.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is available at https://cevalbenchmark.com. The test split labels are kept private to prevent data contamination, and users must submit predictions to the website to obtain accuracy scores. A public leaderboard is maintained.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: C-EVAL aims to help analyze strengths and shortcomings of foundation models in a Chinese context, fostering their development for Chinese users. It addresses the gap in evaluating LLMs in non-English languages and specific cultural contexts.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset focuses on Chinese knowledge, culture, history, and laws, which may exhibit geographical biases towards China compared to English benchmarks. The distribution of correct answers shows small fluctuations around the random 25% level.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset does not cover abilities such as reasoning over APIs, safety, bias, and robustness. The test split labels are not publicly released to prevent data leakage. Some models may struggle with Chain-of-Thought prompting if not specifically tuned for it.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation, Fine Tuning. It is used to evaluate the advanced knowledge and reasoning abilities of foundation models, particularly in a Chinese context.
